Previous admission: 5 days low-grade fever, severe headache, normal head CT, CSF showing lymphocytic pleocytosis (183 cells/µL, 97.8% lymphocytes) and elevated protein (83.3 mg/dL), treated with 9 days IV dexamethasone. The current orthostatic headache pattern raises the possibility of a post-LP CSF leak or ongoing/relapsing CNS inflammation.

The orthostatic pattern strongly suggests a post-LP CSF leak; the tremor and dizziness may relate to ongoing CNS inflammation or steroid effects. Final aetiological diagnosis from the prior admission is still unknown.

36-year-old woman readmitted 3 days after a 12-day admission for lymphocytic meningitis (CSF: 183 cells/µL, 97.8% lymphocytes, protein 83.3 mg/dL; normal head CT). Current presentation: positional headache (worse upright) with meningeal signs (neck stiffness, positive Kernig sign). Meningeal signs make simple post-LP low-pressure headache less likely and raise concern for recurrent/ongoing meningitis or a complication such as cerebral venous sinus thrombosis. Need current investigations to clarify.

36-year-old woman readmitted 3 days after a 12-day admission for lymphocytic meningitis. Current findings: positional headache (worse upright), meningeal signs (neck stiffness, Kernig positive), normal brain MRI, repeat CSF showing persistent lymphocytic pleocytosis (178 cells/µL, 97.7% lymphocytes) but with normalised protein (36.6 mg/dL, down from 83.3). The persistent pleocytosis suggests ongoing meningeal inflammation, while the positional headache and normalised protein raise the possibility of a post-LP low-pressure component superimposed on resolving meningitis. Normal MRI makes structural complications less likely. Need to know prior treatment to assess adequacy of therapy.
